title: An X-HTDC Method for Estimating Particulate Phosphorus from Phytoplankton and Zooplankton
author: Yingyu Hu
materials: Combust dried samples at 800 °C for 09:00:00 Muffle furnace (F30428C, Thermo, 10-505-13) Map the location of crucibles in the oven, in case pencil mark disappears under 800°C. Ramp rate should be controlled at < 200 °C /hour or follow the instruction provided by manufacture, otherwise the crucibles might shatter. SP.RAT: 150/PAMPU: hour Or SP.RAT: 2.5/PAMPU: minute
Standard working solutions and reagents can be prepared during sample digestion.
All reagents are freshly prepared before colorimetric measurement.

2.5 % ammonium molybdate reagent: Weigh 0.25 g ammonium molybdate in a Falcon tube and top to 10 g with MilliQ water. Cap and shake until totally dissolved. Ammonium molybdate Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #09878-100G (CAS: 12054-85-2)

10 % ascorbic acid reagent: Weigh 1 g ascorbic acid in a Falcon tube and top to 10 g with MilliQ water; Cap and shake until all dissolved. Ascorbic acid Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #A5960-100G (CAS: 50-81-7) Wrap the tube with foil if the reagent is not used right after prepared.

Mix the reagents into Falcon tube: For fewer than 60 samples, prepare the final reagent in a 50 mL Falcon tube by adding 17 mL Milli-Q water, followed by 1 mL concentrated sulfuric acid (18 M), then 6 mL of 2.5% ammonium molybdate and 6 mL of 10% ascorbic acid reagent. The same pipette tip can be used to transfer ammonium molybdate and ascorbic acid, as they are mixed into the final reagent.
Read plate in microplate reader Varioskan LUX Multimode Microplate Reader (Thermo Fisher, VL0L00D0)
Other steps are the same as X-HTDC method.

Combust dried samples at 800 °C for 09:00:00 Muffle furnace (F30428C, Thermo, 10-505-13) Map the location of crucibles in the oven, in case pencil mark disappears under 800°C. Ramp rate should be controlled at < 200 °C /hour or follow the instruction provided by manufacture, otherwise the crucibles might shatter. SP.RAT: 150/PAMPU: hour Or SP.RAT: 2.5/PAMPU: minute

steps.title: Acid‑wash and combust GF/F filters
steps.instruction: Place each 25 mm pre‑combusted GF/F filter into a 50 mL Falcon tube, add 0.2 M HCl, cap and shake gently; drain the acid into a beaker containing baking soda for neutralisation. Rinse the filter by adding Milli‑Q water, cap and shake; repeat the rinse and drainage until the rinse water reaches neutral pH (check with pH strip). After the final rinse, transfer the filter and water to a larger acid‑washed beaker, shake for 1 h, then arrange the filters on a watch glass, cover with a second watch glass and dry at 60 °C overnight. Using clean forceps, lift each filter (apply a small amount of 95 % ethanol to the edge if it adheres), place filters overlapping in the base of a borosilicate Petri dish, cover and allow to air‑dry completely.

steps.title: Filter sample onto prepared filter
steps.instruction: Filter microalgae or plankton suspension onto the pre‑treated polycarbonate filter or the pre‑combusted 25 mm GF/F filter using gentle vacuum pressure (5 inches Hg).

steps.title: Add oxalate reagent
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL oxalate reagent onto the filter in the funnel and let it sit for 5 minutes (00:05:00).

steps.title: Rinse filter with saline
steps.instruction: Drain the oxalate solution and rinse the filter once with saline solution (35 g NaCl dissolved in 1 L Milli‑Q water).

steps.title: Freeze filters
steps.instruction: Place each filter into a 2 mL cryogenic vial (Polypropylene, Corning® 66021‑974), seal, flash‑freeze and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Label crucibles and vials
steps.instruction: Mark the lid of each cryogenic vial with an oil‑based white Sharpie and log (1) crucible number and (2) sample code; also label the corresponding porcelain crucible (40 mL, VWR 89037‑996) and its cover (VWR 71000‑146).

steps.title: Transfer filter to crucible
steps.instruction: Using clean filter forceps, transfer the filter into a labeled porcelain crucible and lay the filter flat at the bottom.

steps.title: Dry filters in oven
steps.instruction: Cover the crucibles and place them in a forced‑air oven (VWR 89511‑410) at 90 °C until completely dry; remove promptly. If a muffle furnace is unavailable, keep crucibles in a vacuum desiccator after drying.

steps.title: Cool crucibles gradually
steps.instruction: Allow the dried crucibles to cool gradually inside the muffle furnace.

steps.title: Verify sample markings
steps.instruction: Check the Sharpie markings on each crucible; re‑mark with a general Sharpie if any label is unclear.

steps.title: Prepare 0.2 M HCl reagent
steps.instruction: In a reagent bottle, dilute 12 N HCl with Milli‑Q water at a ratio of 1 part acid to 59 parts water to obtain 0.2 M HCl. Calculate the required volume as 5 mL × (number of samples + number of blanks).

steps.title: Add HCl to crucibles
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of the prepared 0.2 M HCl to each crucible.

steps.title: Arrange crucibles for handling
steps.instruction: Cover the crucibles and place them in a muffin‑tin pan for easier handling; allow the contents to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Homogenise crucible solution
steps.instruction: Aspirate and dispense the solution in each crucible with a pipette three times to ensure homogeneity.

steps.title: Incubate crucibles in oven
steps.instruction: Place the crucibles in an oven and incubate for 30 minutes (00:30:00).

steps.title: Prepare KH₂PO₄ primary standard
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 1 g KH₂PO₄ into a beaker, cover with foil, dry in an oven at 110 °C for at least 2 hours, transfer to a vacuum desiccator, and let cool to room temperature. Dissolve the dried KH₂PO₄ (≈0.136 g) in 1 L Milli‑Q water using a 1 L volumetric flask; record the exact weight used. Transfer the stock solution to a 1 L bottle and store in the refrigerator.

steps.title: Make standard working solutions
steps.instruction: Transfer 500 µL of each standard stock solution into separate 2 mL microtubes.

steps.title: Prepare 6 N sulfuric acid reagent
steps.instruction: Carefully add 1 part 18 M concentrated H₂SO₄ to 5 parts Milli‑Q water to obtain a 6 N (≈3 M) sulfuric acid solution.

steps.title: Calculate molybdate‑ascorbic reagent volume
steps.instruction: Determine total reagent volume as 0.5 mL × (number of standard working solutions + number of samples + number of blanks).

steps.title: Preheat incubator/shaker
steps.instruction: Set the incubator/shaker (Corning LSE 71L) to 37 °C.

steps.title: Add molybdate‑ascorbic reagent
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of the molybdate‑ascorbic reagent to each standard, sample, and blank tube (start with blanks). Before dispensing, wipe or dab the liquid drop on the outside of the tip to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Mix reaction tubes
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube briefly to mix.

steps.title: Incubate colour development
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes at 37 °C while shaking at 200 rpm for 3 hours (03:00:00).

steps.title: Load microplate
steps.instruction: Transfer 250 µL of each reaction mixture into a 96‑well clear polystyrene microplate (Greiner Bio‑One 655101) in duplicate.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 820 nm
steps.instruction: Read the absorbance of each well at 820 nm using a plate reader.

steps.title: Blank‑correct standard absorbance
steps.instruction: Subtract the average absorbance of the blank standard replicates from the absorbance of each standard working solution.

steps.title: Blank‑correct sample absorbance
steps.instruction: Subtract the average absorbance of the blank sample (blank filter) replicates from the absorbance of each unknown sample.

steps.title: Generate standard curve
steps.instruction: Plot the blank‑corrected 820 nm absorbance of each standard versus its concentration (µM) to create a standard curve.

steps.title: Determine orthophosphate concentration
steps.instruction: Use the standard curve to calculate the orthophosphate concentration (µM) of each unknown sample from its blank‑corrected absorbance.

steps.title: Calculate phosphorus per sample
steps.instruction: Compute phosphorus mass per sample (µg) with: P (µg) = orthophosphate (µM) × V_HCl (mL) × 0.001 × 30.97.

steps.title: Weigh zooplankton samples
steps.instruction: Weigh ground, oven‑dried zooplankton material directly into labelled porcelain crucibles.

steps.title: Prepare 0.034 M MgSO₄ reagent
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.023 g anhydrous MgSO₄ (CAS 7487‑88‑9) in 250 mL Milli‑Q water to make a 0.034 M solution; for GF/F filters use 24 g MgSO₄ in 100 mL to make a 2 M solution (heat may cause boiling).

steps.title: Add MgSO₄ to samples
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of the 0.034 M MgSO₄ reagent to each PC‑filter sample or zooplankton sample; add 1.6 mL of the 2 M MgSO₄ reagent to each GF/F‑filter sample.

steps.title: Centrifuge hydrolysate
steps.instruction: Transfer 2 mL of the hydrolysate from each sample to a microtube and centrifuge at 13 000 rpm for 5 minutes (temperature not specified) to pellet MgSiO₃ crystals and debris.

steps.title: Prepare final assay aliquots
steps.instruction: Transfer 500 µL of the supernatant to a new 2 mL microtube; duplicate each sample and its corresponding blank before proceeding with the colour‑development assay described in steps 15‑24.
